name: Dyad
license: Apache 2.0 (the src/pro directory is under the Functional Source License 1.1, Apache 2.0 future license)
summary: A free, open-source desktop app builder: you chat with the model of your choice, and it writes a React or Next.js app into a local Git repository and runs it on your own machine.
intro: Dyad is an Electron app for macOS, Windows and Linux (experimental) that does what Lovable or v0 do, but locally. Each app is a regular folder, by default under `~/dyad-apps/<app-name>`, holding a JavaScript project built from a template: a minimal React and Vite app by default, or Next.js with shadcn/ui and Tailwind. Dyad runs it with your own Node.js and shows a live preview next to the chat. Every edit the AI makes becomes a Git commit with an AI-written message, and restoring an old version adds a revert commit, so history is never lost and you can open the same repository in VS Code at any time.

You bring the model. Dyad calls OpenAI, Anthropic or Google with your own API keys, OpenRouter, or a local model through Ollama or LM Studio, so the code and prompts go only where you send them. For backends it connects to Supabase or Neon; for deployment it pushes to GitHub, and Vercel or another host builds from there. Build mode applies one generation at a time; Agent mode keeps a task list, reads server and browser logs and fixes its own errors. A basic Agent mode is free for 20 messages a day.

The code outside `src/pro` is Apache 2.0. Dyad Pro ($20 a month, 200 AI credits) and Dyad Max ($79 a month, 900 credits) add the full Agent mode and two cost savers: Turbo Edits, which hands routine file edits to a faster, cheaper model, and Smart Context, which uses a small model to pick the relevant files instead of sending the whole codebase.
strengths: No lock-in: apps are plain Git repositories on your disk, and you can switch to another editor or tool at any time
Any model, including free tiers such as Google’s Gemini API and offline local models
Free to use with your own keys, with no sign-up and no limit on the number of projects
Open source and built in public, with signed releases built directly on GitHub
limits: JavaScript apps only: no other languages, and mobile apps only as hybrid web apps
You run everything: Node.js must be installed, and hosting, databases and API costs are yours to arrange
The best agent features (full Agent mode, Turbo Edits, Smart Context) are in the paid Pro tier, under a source-available license
Linux support is experimental and untested, without auto-updates

story: Will Chen created Dyad as a local, open-source alternative to cloud app builders such as Lovable, v0 and Bolt. The idea, in Chen’s words, was that builders should feel like owners, not renters: the code stays on their computer, they choose the model, and nothing is locked into a hosted platform. The first public releases came in April 2025; version 0.1.7 on 22 April simplified onboarding and added opt-in telemetry.

Through frequent releases, Dyad added Supabase and Neon integrations, MCP servers, a security review, imports of existing apps, hybrid mobile apps, Agent mode and a paid Pro tier whose code lives in a separate, fair-source directory. Version 1.0.0 shipped on 19 May 2026, after a year of development, with a redesigned app sidebar and Neon support for Vite and Nitro projects. Version 1.19.0 followed on 12 October 2026, by which time the repository had more than 21,000 GitHub stars.

choices.choice: Run locally instead of in the cloud
choices.why: Chen wanted users to own their apps rather than rent them: projects live on disk as ordinary Git repositories, and with a local model even prompts never leave the machine.
Letting users pick any provider, including free tiers and local models, avoids locking them into one vendor’s model or pricing.

choices.choice: Open core with a fair-source Pro directory
choices.why: The free builder stays under Apache 2.0, while the paid Pro features, kept in `src/pro`, are fair source: published under the Functional Source License 1.1 with Apache 2.0 as its future license.
